findings.passage: A month after an investor asked him to sound more positive, he made the case for slowing down in public and committed his own company first.
findings.problem: Coverage gap in the pacing timeline. Fortune (Beatrice Nolan, July 29, 2026, https://fortune.com/2026/07/29/anthropic-deepmind-openai-meta-washington-ai-slowdown-plan/, opened this session) reports that the cross-lab 'Pacing the Frontier' statement, published Tuesday July 28, 2026, was signed by Amodei and several Anthropic co-founders. It asks the U.S. government to help build tools to slow AI development if that becomes necessary. His Aug 15 X reply to Baker (S10, opened in research) defends 'the "Pacing the Frontier" letter'. The section jumps from July 2025 to September 2026, so this sentence can read as his first public pacing stance. The Type 5 section's 'His 2026 turn on pacing came as his own model updating' (C128) also omits that the turn first surfaced as a co-signed collective statement to government. Nothing stated is false; the September essay was his first call to slow now.
findings.acceptance_test: The evidence record adds the July 28, 2026 statement with an opened source. The pacing section gets one dated clause placing it between the July 2025 condition and the September 2026 essay. The investor sentence no longer implies the essay was his first public pacing position, and C128's Five-leaning reading is re-tested against the co-signed statement.

findings.passage: Greg Diamos, who hired him, told AFP
findings.problem: S01 says Ng reached out to Amodei and Diamos, 'an early member of the team', 'encouraged the team to hire him'. AFP (S14) says Diamos reviewed his application and code. 'Who hired him' makes him the hiring decision-maker.
findings.acceptance_test: Reword to what the sources support, e.g., 'Greg Diamos, an early Baidu team member who pushed to hire him, told AFP'.

findings.passage: OpenAI and xAI had accepted terms allowing "all lawful purposes," so refusing them made Anthropic the Journal's "healthy alternative."
findings.problem: The clause rests on Fortune's Feb 27, 2026 report (S18). AP (S19, same day) reports that hours later Altman announced a classified Pentagon deal and said it enshrined prohibitions on domestic mass surveillance and required human responsibility for the use of force. Undated, the clause can leave readers thinking OpenAI's eventual terms had none of Anthropic's limits.
findings.acceptance_test: Date the clause to Fortune's Feb 27 report (e.g., 'as Fortune reported that day') or add one clause noting Altman's claim about OpenAI's deal; the commercial reading can stay.
